title: Managing Up, Down and Across
overview: Transitioning into a managerial or supervisory role presents new challenges and responsibilities. As management practices evolve, continuous guidance and skill enhancement become essential. Today’s managers and supervisors face multifaceted challenges, navigating relationships and expectations not only with their superiors but also with their subordinates and peers. Many new managers find this transition difficult and often encounter unexpected obstacles. This course provides new managers and supervisors with a solid foundation to thrive in their roles, ensuring they achieve the performance and results they envisioned when accepting their new positions.
audience: This course is tailored for new managers and supervisors across all industries who seek to establish a strong foundation in their management roles.
methodology: Participants will engage in extensive role-playing of real-life business scenarios through case studies, allowing them to practice recommended approaches. Self-assessments will also be a key component, helping participants gain insights into their personal management styles and attitudes.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Gain a deeper understanding of their strengths, weaknesses, and attitudes
Build strong, positive relationships with their direct managers
Effectively manage and develop their direct reports
Foster professional relationships with peers and influence them effectively
Understand and positively influence the organizational culture
